page: The Amazon Web Services c8ib.32xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized server instance managed by the AWS Nitro System. Hardware resources include 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel processors operating at a frequency of 3.9 GHz, utilizing simultaneous multithreading at two threads per core. System memory is sized at 256.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per core or 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation. The platform does not feature integrated graphics or discrete hardware accelerators, maintaining a zero GPU configuration.

A prominent architectural component of the c8ib.32xlarge is its networking layer, supplying a baseline network bandwidth of 133 Gbps. This throughput facilitates high-bandwidth inter-node communication across clustered topologies. Unlike instances containing local solid-state drives, this server allocates zero bundled local storage. All persistent disk operations must route over the network to external block devices. This stateless configuration avoids allocating budget to local ephemeral drives when persistent storage is preferred, though it shifts storage I/O entirely onto network interfaces.

From a resource density perspective, the platform emphasizes dedicated thread count and network capacity over memory expansion or attached storage arrays. Workloads constrained by CPU clock cycles and node-to-node communications achieve high resource efficiency, whereas memory-saturated tasks or deep learning acceleration will encounter architectural limits. The c8ib.32xlarge is targeted for distributed high-performance computing, large-scale batch processing, scientific simulations, continuous integration suites, and clustered data transformation pipelines.
description: The Amazon Web Services c8ib.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro system, powered by x86_64 Intel processors operating at 3.9 GHz. It provides 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 64 physical cores with two threads per core, alongside 256.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio. This instance features an extensive baseline network bandwidth of 133 Gbps, making it suited for tightly coupled parallel computation and network-bound processing tasks. It includes zero discrete GPUs and provides no bundled local storage, necessitating reliance on networked storage architectures for persistent data. By dedicating resources purely to high clock-rate processing and massive network throughput rather than attached NVMe drives or accelerator hardware, the configuration yields targeted efficiency for scale-out compute environments. The c8ib.32xlarge is well tailored for high-performance computing clusters, distributed batch analytics, scientific modeling, ETL data processing, and compute-heavy enterprise applications.
